winner.title: Ndolé with Beef and Shrimp (Cameroonian Bitterleaf stew)

evidence.authenticity: Uses real ndole leaves (boiled twice for 15 min to remove bitterness), peanuts, crayfish, smoked fish, beef and shrimp, palm oil finish (Douala-style surf and turf). Ties dish to Cameroon Unity Day and lists related greens (okok, eru). Author not stated to be Cameroonian.
evidence.precision: Grams for 6 of 13 ingredients (650g beef, 350g shrimp, 300g peanuts, 60g ginger, 100g fish); doneness cues on about 6 of 14 steps (brown, tender, translucent, pink, paste-like); only 'large pot' and 'smaller pot'; no temperatures; leaf boil has time only.
evidence.testing: No test kitchen. Some reasoning: double boil to cut bitterness, tender smoked cod instead of hard fish, crayfish powdered, peanuts may be soaked overnight. Rate not shown.
evidence.photos: WebFetch: photos show ingredients and finished dish only, plus a video; no step photos.
evidence.efficiency: Prep 20 min, cook 1h40, total 2h stated. Parallel work (peanuts and meat) is implied. Serves 8.
evidence.access: Frozen ndole leaves from African stores; no leaf substitute given. Other items at grocery stores.

winner.why: Best balance of traditional method and gram weights, but still under 60 because it has no step photos and little testing evidence.

runnerUp.title: Ndolé, the recipe for Cameroon's national dish

evidence.authenticity: Dried ndole leaves, peanut paste, dried shrimp, smoked fish, red palm oil; double boil of leaves; cites Cameroon national dish context.
evidence.precision: Metric weights for 6 of 13 ingredients; few doneness cues (1); times only for most steps.
evidence.testing: No sign of testing; brief tip on a second boil for lighter bitterness.
evidence.photos: No step images in schema; 59 images on page are likely product shots and not confirmed as process photos.
evidence.access: Dried ndole leaves sold by the retailer; no substitute given.

runnerUp.why: Clear structure and metric amounts, but a retailer page with fewer cues and no step photos.

searches: node scripts/recipe-hunt.mjs sites "Ndole" (no matches on any of the 4 sites)
notes: No test-kitchen version exists on Serious Eats, NYT, ATK or BBC. All candidates are blogs with no step photos and weak precision. Immaculate Bites and Eat Well Abi use spinach as a main or partial leaf, which departs from the traditional dish. Wikibooks, preciouscore and congocookbook were surfaced by search but not read. If a retry is wanted, read those.
